description: MCP server for Claude (Claude in Chrome, claude.ai): save Facebook posts to NocoDB content_ideation.facebook_posts and search them for content ideation.
name: Content ideation MCP

parameters.instructions:
Tools for the user's library of Facebook posts kept as references for content ideation (NocoDB table content_ideation.facebook_posts).

Before save_facebook_post: expand "See more" so the text is complete. Save comments in this markdown format: (N reactions) and the commenter's name on one line, the comment text below, replies as indented '- ' items in the same shape, and --- between top-level comments:
(120 reactions) Commenter Name
Comment text
  - (8 reactions) Reply Author
    Reply text
---
(45 reactions) Commenter Name
Next comment text

Use find_facebook_posts to pull references when the user brainstorms content.

value.author_name: ={{ $fromAI('author_name', `Name of the page, person or group member who posted.`, 'string') }}
value.author_url: ={{ $fromAI('author_url', `Profile or page URL of the author, without query parameters.`, 'string') }}
value.comment_count: ={{ $fromAI('comment_count', `Total comments as an integer (1.2K = 1200). 0 if not shown.`, 'number') }}
value.comments:
={{ $fromAI('comments', `Visible comments as markdown. Each comment is (N reactions) and the commenter's name on one line, then the comment text on the next. Replies go under their comment as indented '- ' list items in the same shape. A line with --- separates top-level comments. Example:
(120 reactions) Commenter Name
Comment text
  - (8 reactions) Reply Author
    Reply text
---
(45 reactions) Commenter Name
Next comment text
Empty string if there are no comments.`, 'string') }}
value.format: ={{ $fromAI('format', `One of: text, image, carousel, video, reel, link, live.`, 'string') }}
value.hook: ={{ $fromAI('hook', `First line of the post text, as written.`, 'string') }}
value.post_url: ={{ $fromAI('post_url', `Canonical permalink of the post, such as https://www.facebook.com/<page>/posts/<id>, https://www.facebook.com/groups/<group>/posts/<id> or https://www.facebook.com/reel/<id>. Remove tracking query parameters.`, 'string') }}
value.posted_at: ={{ $fromAI('posted_at', `Publish time as ISO 8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-09-15T08:30:00+07:00. Read the exact time from the timestamp tooltip. Empty string if unknown.`, 'string') }}
value.reaction_count: ={{ $fromAI('reaction_count', `Total reactions as an integer (1.2K = 1200). 0 if not shown.`, 'number') }}
value.share_count: ={{ $fromAI('share_count', `Total shares as an integer (1.2K = 1200). 0 if not shown.`, 'number') }}
value.source_type: ={{ $fromAI('source_type', `Where the post lives: page, profile or group.`, 'string') }}
value.text: ={{ $fromAI('text', `Full post text after expanding See more, keeping line breaks and emoji.`, 'string') }}
value.why_it_works: ={{ $fromAI('why_it_works', `Short analysis of why the post performs: hook, structure, angle, emotional trigger, call to action, and what the comments reveal about the audience.`, 'string') }}

parameters.toolDescription: Save one Facebook post (text, engagement, comments) as a content reference. Always appends a new row.

options.where: ={{ $fromAI('where', `NocoDB filter. Examples: (post_url,eq,https://www.facebook.com/x/posts/1) ; (text,like,%keyword%)~or(hook,like,%keyword%) ; (reaction_count,gt,1000)~and(format,eq,reel). Use (post_url,isnot,null) to list everything.`, 'string') }}

parameters.toolDescription: Search saved Facebook reference posts, newest capture first. Columns: post_url, hook, author_name, author_url, source_type, posted_at, format, text, reaction_count, comment_count, share_count, comments, why_it_works, notes, captured_at.
